chunks: Al-Naḍr ibn Suwayd narrated from ʿAbdullāh ibn Sinān, from Abū ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

When the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم recited the talbiyah, he said: ‘Labbayka Allahumma labbayk, labbayka la sharika laka labbayk, indeed all praise and blessing are Yours, and the kingdom; there is no partner for You, labbayk. Labbayka, O Possessor of the Ascents, labbayk.’

And he عليه السلام would frequently repeat ‘Dhī al-Maʿārij,’ and he would recite the talbiyah whenever he met a rider, ascended a hill, descended into a valley, in the latter part of the night, and after the prayers.

key_terms.النِّعْمَةَ: Blessing and bounty belonging to Allah.
key_terms.الْمُلْكَ: Sovereignty and dominion belonging to Allah.
key_terms.ذَا الْمَعَارِجِ: Possessor of the ascents; a divine description used in the talbiyah.
key_terms.لَا شَرِيكَ لَكَ: An affirmation that Allah has no partner.
key_terms.لَبَّيْكَ: A formula of response and devotion meaning: I answer Your call.

ai.seo_question: What wording did the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم use for the talbiyah, and when would he repeat it?
ai.summary: This hadith records the talbiyah of the Messenger of Allah صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم and highlights its wording affirming tawhid, praise, blessing, and dominion for Allah alone. It also shows the sunnah of frequently repeating the talbiyah during hajj-related movement and at recurring moments such as the end of the night and after salat (prayer).

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.2578 - Al-Nadr ibn Suwayd narrated from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Abdullah (as), who said:

"When the Messenger of Allah (swt) (peace be upon him and his family) recited the Talbiyah, he said:
'Labbayka Allahumma Labbayk, Labbayka la sharika laka Labbayk, Inna al-hamda wa al-ni'mata laka wa al-mulk, la sharika laka Labbayk. Labbayka Dhal-Ma'arij Labbayk.'

Prophet (sw) frequently repeated Dhal-Ma'arij and would recite the Talbiyah whenever he met a rider, ascended a hill, descended into a valley, during the last part of the night, and after the prayers."
